application.cv_markdown:
Sofia Larsen
Signal Processing Engineer

EDUCATION

Kallavesi University of Technology — MSc, Electrical Engineering, 2006

EXPERIENCE

Tuulikallio Embedded Systems — Signal Processing Engineer
2007 – present

- RF front-end characterisation and calibration for X-band and Ku-band receiver modules. Responsible for the company’s semi-annual calibration campaigns using Keysight PNA-X vector network analysers and N9040B spectrum analysers, including S-parameter measurement, gain flatness verification, and noise-figure characterisation across temperature in a controlled RF test facility.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Tundra SAR Processor (Tuulikallio, 2015–2018)
Implemented the range-compression and azimuth-focusing kernels in C++ for a real-time SAR image processor running on a custom FPGA/DSP hybrid board (Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+). Achieved per-pulse processing within a 5-microsecond budget. The C++ codebase comprises approximately 15,000 lines and runs in production at two customer sites.

Tundra-QA (Tuulikallio, ongoing)
Developed and maintained Tundra-QA, a Python quality-assurance and regression-testing framework for the SAR processor product line. Used in production by four engineers for automated calibration-data validation and nightly regression runs. Includes CI integration with GitLab and structured test reports. Approximately 6,000 lines of tested code.

Master’s Thesis (Kallavesi University of Technology, 2006)
“Wideband channel sounding for millimetre-wave indoor propagation.” Built and operated a 60 GHz sliding-correlator channel sounder in Kallavesi’s radio laboratory, collecting delay-spread and angular-spread measurements in office and corridor environments. The thesis applied radio-propagation theory and statistical modelling to a practical measurement campaign, demonstrating the degree’s direct relevance to applied RF and signal-processing engineering.

SKILLS

- Phased-array signal processing: designed and simulated 16-element and 64-element receive beamforming architectures for X-band and Ku-band radar applications using custom MATLAB tooling and validated against measured array data.
- Kalman filtering and estimation theory: designed and tuned an extended Kalman filter for multi-sensor target tracking in a coastal-surveillance radar prototype, validated against recorded ship-traffic data from a Baltic Sea field trial (2020).
- Languages: English (professional working language since 2007; all technical documentation, design reviews, and customer communication at Tuulikallio is conducted in English), Finnish (native), Swedish (conversational).
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Hiring Manager,

This application is for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara Oy. I have spent nineteen years at Tuulikallio Embedded Systems building real-time signal-processing systems from algorithm design through to field-deployed hardware, and the technical scope of this role — SAR payloads, scatterometer electronics, ground-segment processing chains — aligns closely with my working experience. My strength is in the full lifecycle: taking a processing algorithm from simulation through embedded implementation to a tested, delivered system that works under operational conditions. I would like to outline what I think I would bring.

The deliverable I am most satisfied with at Tuulikallio is the Tundra SAR processor, which I took from a MATLAB prototype through to a production C++ implementation running on a Zynq UltraScale+ board with a per-pulse budget of 5 microseconds. The implementation handles range compression, azimuth focusing, and motion compensation in a streaming architecture that processes each range line before the next pulse arrives. That system is now deployed at two customer sites and has been in continuous field operation since 2018. I then built the Python regression-testing framework that keeps it honest: Tundra-QA runs nightly against the production codebase and catches regressions before they reach a customer. Between the two, I have a clear example of what I mean by “algorithm to delivered product.”

When Tuulikallio won the Polarfront coastal-radar contract in 2019, I was asked to lead the five-person signal-processing team for the programme. Over fourteen months I ran weekly design reviews, managed the work breakdown and schedule, allocated tasks across three work packages, and coordinated integration testing across the DSP, firmware, and RF subsystem teams. We delivered the acceptance-tested system two weeks ahead of the contractual deadline, and the customer accepted it without a single open defect. That programme taught me that I enjoy the coordination and planning side of engineering as much as the hands-on implementation, and it is a responsibility I would want to carry into my next role.

On the practical question of location: my partner’s family is from Oulu, and we have been planning a move north for the past year. This role gives me the chance to align professional and personal geography, which is part of why I am writing now rather than waiting. I am already familiar with the city and have spent extended periods there.

Kaikuvaara’s position in Oulu’s remote-sensing cluster and the company’s focus on instrument-level processing are well matched to the experience I have built. I am used to working in small engineering teams with tight schedules and hardware deadlines, and I expect the transition would be straightforward. I am happy to discuss specifics at your convenience.

Yours sincerely,
Sofia Larsen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
